Class OwnHost

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.host.OwnHost
public final class OwnHost extends Object
The panel host of a library's own screen: a screen class a library ships (a custom container screen, say) that lays out its own panels the way MKScreen does, with the main panel as the frame, and joins MenuKit's claims, modals and draw order with them. Panels other mods inject onto the screen (adapters, anchors) are hosted by MenuKit as on any screen; this host holds only the screen's own.

The screen drives it: layout() each frame (its main panel's rectangle becomes the screen's image), renderFlow(GuiGraphicsExtractor, int, int) before vanilla's content pass, the input methods from its own handlers, and attach() and detach() from init and removed. Popover and overlay panels draw above vanilla's slots through MenuKit's container-screen layers, with no call from the screen. 

host = OwnHost.of(this, ScreenKind.PANEL, OwnHost.TitleBand.IN_FRAME)
        .slotOwnership(this::ownsSlotAt);
for (Panel p : panels) host.add(p, p.interiorPadding());

    • add

      public void add(Panel panel, int padding)
      Adds a panel by its own placements (Panel.placements(), 7.4.0), one per mode scope; each frame it takes the current mode's, else its BOTH one. Panels order by their priority, then by the order they were added. A panel with no placement takes the standalone default in both modes: the main panel when this host has none yet, else region(BOTTOM_CENTER) PanelPosition.STANDALONE_STACK_GAP below the one before (add a declared main() first).
      Parameters:
      padding - content padding between the panel's edge and its elements
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - for a placement on an anchor (put an anchored panel on with an AnchorPanelAdapter), or one this host can't place

    • add

      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Replaced in 7.4.0 by add(Panel, int), which reads where the panel goes in each mode from its placements; removed in 8.0.0. This is position in both modes, whatever placements the panel declares.
      Adds a panel at position, in both modes. Panels order by their priority, then by the order they were added.
      Parameters:
      position - the position to place it at (the panel's own, or a default the screen picks for an unplaced one)
      padding - content padding between the panel's edge and its elements
